meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the PTA-FC unit
meta.scope: From the R-101 outlet flange (72 bar a, 285 °C) through PCV-102 / XV-105, the four flash crystallizers V-201 … V-204 with their agitators, the vapour risers to the four headers and E-211 … E-241, the purge water from its pump, to the product line at the slurry receiver (4 bar a). R-101 and its relief, the steam users, the flare and the centrifuge house are interfaces.
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: Design case: 250 t/h of 30 wt% TA solution at 285 °C; V-201 … V-204 at 48.66 / 34.47 / 23.09 / 10.85 bar a and 269.5 / 243.5 / 218.1 / 180.0 °C. Trained operators. Instruments and trips are proof tested yearly (LOPA tab). Risk matrix and target event frequencies are the example values of the HAZID and LOPA tabs; PFDs are teaching defaults in the CCPS style.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N2.causes:
PIC-210 in MAN with PCV-210 closed
PCV-210 stuck while the charge rises
header back-pressure 38 → 47.5 bar a (E-211 fouled: PCV-210 at 100 %)
N2.cons: With PCV-210 closed the pressure reaches 53 bar a in 7.5 min (PSHH-218 trip, 276.7 °C) and PSV-217 is not reached; with the header backed up V-201 floats at 50.2 bar a and +2.6 °C with no trip, V-201 crystallizes less and V-202 more; worst case overpressure of V-201

N2.causes:
PCV-210 fails open (instrument air)
PIC-210 in MAN open
PT-210 reads high
N2.cons: V-201 drops toward the 38 bar header: flash surge with entrainment of slurry into the vapour line, the temperature falls to about 248 °C so V-201 crystallizes far more (high supersaturation, nucleation, fines) and the ΔP to V-202 shrinks

N2.causes:
LCV-211 stuck or LIC-211 in MAN closed
LT-211 reads low (nozzle plugged without purge water)
charge raised with a stuck valve (80.7 % in 30 min)
N2.cons: With LCV-211 shut the level reaches 92 % in 5.4 min (LSHH-215 trip); above 93 % slurry is carried into the vapour line and plugs PCV-210 and E-211; a plugged LT reads low while the true level climbs
N2.notes:
Worked example
LOPA (LOPA tab, scenario L2): IE LIC-211 loop failure 0.1 /yr; LI-211 HI alarm not credited (2 min to carry-over); LSHH-215 → XV-105 (SIF-05, PFD ≈ 0.045) credited. TEL for S4 = 10⁻³ /yr.

ie.d: LIC-211 loop failure or LCV-211 stuck closed

N2.causes:
LIC-211 in MAN with LCV-211 wide open
LT-211 reads high
feed lost with LCV-211 open
N2.cons: The level falls to 5 % in 15 min: LSLL-216 forces LCV-211 closed and the valve cycles every 2.3 min; the surge of hot slurry drives V-202 to 36 bar a (PI-220 HI); if the seal is lost, 48.7 bar steam blows through LCV-211 into V-202 (34.5 bar a) toward PSHH-228

N2.causes:
Pressure high (see MORE pressure)
feed hotter
PT-210 frozen while the header backs up (PIC-210 does not act, TI-212 climbs)
N2.cons: Less crystallized in V-201 and more in V-202 (V-202 flash supersaturation rises, fines); a frozen PT leaves PI-210 on its set point while TI-212 drifts 5 °C

N2.causes:
Pressure low
purge water set high (FIC-213 SP 5 t/h of 40 °C water)
feed cold
N2.cons: More TA crystallizes in V-201 at higher supersaturation (fines); dilution raises the TA lost in the mother liquor

N2.dev: Vapour leaving other than through PCV-210
N2.causes:
PSV-217 passing after a lift
PSV-217 set drift
N2.cons: Steam at 269 °C goes to the flare instead of the 38 bar header; PIC-210 holds the pressure by closing PCV-210, so FI-219 falls while PI-210 stays on set point; TA fines deposit in the flare line

N2.causes:
Motor trip
power dip (all four agitators)
N2.cons: Crystals settle (87 % settled in 30 min): the outlet thickens, the mean size falls (AI-253 120 → 106 µm), the product thins (DI-254 32.5 wt%); a restart into the settled bed trips the motor on overload

N2.dev: M-201 running slowly or impeller worn
N2.causes:
Belt slip
impeller erosion
low speed selected
N2.cons: Local settling in the bottom head; coarser, less uniform crystals; higher outlet solids

N2.causes:
Entrainment at high level or on a pressure dip
foaming
N2.cons: TA solids foul PCV-210 and E-211 and erode the valve trim; the header steam users receive TA in the condensate

N2.causes:
Agitator seal failure after the seal flush is lost
LCV-211 body erosion at 14 bar ΔP with slurry
nozzle flange leak
N2.cons: Slurry at 269 °C and 48.7 bar a flashes to steam and TA dust: burns, a steam cloud with hydrogen traces, loss of the vessel inventory until XV-105 and LCV-211 are closed

sg.text: PSHH-218 53 bar a (2 s) closes XV-105
FIC-213 purge keeps the nozzle clear
FI-219 vs the flash heat balance
XSL-214 agitator stopped > 10 min with feed closes XV-105
JI-214 (current falls with a worn impeller)

recs.text: On PSHH-2k8 also close the upstream level valve LCV-2(k−1)1: a feed trip alone does not stop the pressure rise when the vapour outlet is blocked, because the cascade from the hotter vessel keeps flashing (V-204 reached 15.1 bar a and PSV-247 lifted 1.8 min after the PSHH-248 trip in the simulator).

Verify PSV-217..247 sizing for the blocked vapour outlet case at full flash duty (V-201 31.6 t/h steam at design) and for the cascade case (hot slurry from the upstream vessel flashing into a vessel whose PCV is closed); record the governing case.

Add header pressure alarms upstream of E-211..E-241 and an operating instruction to cut the charge when a PCV-2k0 reaches 95 % output (PCV-210 is at 100 % with the header at 47.5 bar a; margin to PSHH-218 is then 2.8 bar).

Carry-over protection: check the vapour-space velocity at 85 % level against the entrainment limit, consider a demister or a vortex breaker in the vapour nozzle, and alarm on PCV-2k0 output change at constant flow (fouling by solids).

On LSHH-2k5 (92 %) also close the level valve of the vessel upstream (LCV-2(k−1)1) or trip LIC-2(k−1)1 to 0 %: after XV-105 closes, the upstream vessels keep cascading hot slurry into the full vessel (the simulator shows V-202 at 97 % and carry-over 3 min after the LSHH-225 trip).
Make LSHH-2k5 independent of the LT-2k1 nozzle that plugs without purge water: separate nozzle with its own purge, or a different technology (nuclear / guided-wave radar); confirm in the SRS.
Level measurement integrity: periodic comparison of LI-2k1 with a material-balance level (FI-255 against the LCV opening), calibration of LT-241, and a procedure for a level that stops moving.
Vapour blow-through: confirm LSLL-2k6 is an independent switch tested yearly, and add a low limit on the LIC-2k1 output so a single transmitter error cannot drain the seal.
Add a DCS consistency check per vessel, T − [Tsat(P) + BPE], with a ±2 °C alarm: it exposes a transmitter bias (PT-230 low, TI-222 high) or a frozen PT-210 that the single-loop alarms do not see.
Frozen-signal and rate-of-change diagnostics on PT-210..240 and LT-211..241 (HART / DCS bad-PV handling); a frozen PT leaves PIC in control of a wrong number.
PSV passing detection: temperature on each PSV tail pipe and a heat-balance check of FI-2k9 against the flash duty on the DCS.
Flare system: confirm the flare header and knock-out drum accept the simultaneous lift of PSV-217..247 (steam with TA fines that deposit on cooling) and heat-trace the KO drum and tail pipes.

Review the 10-min XSL agitator-stopped delay against the settling rate: the product thickened to DI-254 HI (50 wt%) 9.5 min after M-203 stopped and the bed was 97 % settled at 30 min; consider 5 min for V-203/V-204 and a restart interlock that checks the settled bed.
Agitator drives: ride-through (VFD / UPS for controls) or automatic restart within 60 s after a power dip while the bed is still fluid; four agitators lost together is a common-cause event.

Hot-slurry containment: insulation and guards on every surface above 60 °C, remote isolation (XV-105) from the field, PPE for sample points and nozzle rodding, and a written double-isolation rule for work on a vessel nozzle.
Agitator seals: seal-flush low-flow alarm with a timed stop of the agitator, and a procedure to stop the agitator before the seal runs dry.
